sources.title: Spatial validation and biased occurrences
sources.text: Mosquito occurrence observations can reflect sampling effort. Spatially separated validation blocks help assess transfer to unsampled locations. Random splits may overestimate performance when nearby observations are dependent.

sources.title: Presence-background habitat modeling
sources.text: MaxEnt is a presence-background species distribution method. Background selection and observation bias affect interpretation. Habitat suitability is not disease incidence and does not establish transmission risk.

sources.title: Environmental predictor readiness
sources.text: Temperature and precipitation are candidate environmental predictors for Aedes aegypti habitat suitability. Predictor units, spatial resolution, temporal coverage and study region must match the occurrence observations.

sources.title: Decision formulation
sources.text: A surveillance allocation decision requires an objective, alternatives, information needs and explicit uncertainty. Compare habitat modeling approaches against the geographic and temporal decision context.

sources.title: Unreviewed extraction example
sources.text: A proposed literature extraction suggests that every mosquito habitat map directly predicts human disease burden. This deliberately unsupported teaching assertion must remain a candidate.
